recent_posts.title: Anthropic partners with SpaceX to double Claude Code rate limits
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic has leased over 300 MW of compute capacity at SpaceX's Colossus 1 data center, gaining access to 220,000+ NVIDIA H100 GPUs. The deal was driven by Anthropic severely underestimating demand — projecting 10x annualized growth but experiencing 80x, largely due to Claude Code adoption. Immediate user-facing changes include doubled five-hour rate limits for Claude Code on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans, removal of peak-hour throttling for Pro and Max users, and higher Opus API rate limits. The deal is notable given the awkward history between the companies — Anthropic had cut off xAI's API access and Elon Musk had called Anthropic 'evil' months prior. For xAI, renting out idle Colossus 1 capacity (after migrating to Colossus 2) raises questions about whether it's pivoting toward a neocloud business model rather than pure AI development.

recent_posts.title: reMarkable Paper Pure: a monochrome E Ink notepad that replaces the reMarkable 2
recent_posts.summary: reMarkable has announced the Paper Pure, a $399 monochrome E Ink tablet replacing the six-year-old reMarkable 2. It features a 10.3-inch Carta 1300 panel at 226 PPI, 50% improved responsiveness, 32GB storage (4x the predecessor), and a 3,820 mAh battery rated for up to three weeks. New software features include Google Calendar and Outlook sync, cloud document import, improved handwriting search, Slack integration, and Miro integration. The reMarkable 2 is being retired from production but will continue receiving software support. Notably, reMarkable chose to skip color E Ink despite competitor moves in that direction, doubling down on the monochrome writing experience. The company reports 3.5 million devices sold and 1.2 million Connect subscribers.

recent_posts.title: New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma kills Copilot on consoles and reshuffles leadership
recent_posts.summary: Asha Sharma, the new Xbox CEO replacing Phil Spencer, has cancelled Copilot development on consoles and wound down its Xbox mobile app integration, citing a poor fit with Xbox's direction. She is reshuffling leadership by bringing in executives from Microsoft's CoreAI, GitHub, Meta, and ChatGPT to accelerate development and reduce friction. Key changes include Jason Ronald leading Project Helix (the next Xbox console), Jared Palmer focusing on developer tooling, lowered Game Pass prices, retirement of the 'This is an Xbox' marketing campaign, and a return to the classic green logo. The move is notable as it bucks the trend of talent flowing toward AI teams.

recent_posts.title: Five major publishers sue Meta over Llama training data, allege Zuckerberg personally authorized infringement
recent_posts.summary: Five major publishers — Elsevier, Cengage, Hachette, Macmillan, and McGraw Hill — have filed a class action lawsuit against Meta and CEO Mark Zuckerberg, alleging Meta pirated millions of copyrighted books and journal articles to train its Llama AI models, with Zuckerberg personally authorizing the infringement. Unlike the earlier Kadrey v. Meta case Meta won on fair-use grounds, this suit focuses on academic and educational works with more measurable market harm, and cites Meta's own licensing deals with other publishers as evidence of bad faith. Anthropic's $1.5 billion settlement with authors in 2025 sets a financial benchmark for settlement talks. The outcome could reshape whether AI developers can legally train on unlicensed text, potentially forcing the industry toward structured licensing markets.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft Edge keeps all saved passwords decrypted in process memory by design
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft Edge decrypts all saved passwords at browser startup and keeps them in plaintext in process memory for the entire session — not just when credentials are actively used. A Norwegian security researcher published a proof-of-concept demonstrating that anyone with admin access can dump Edge's process memory and retrieve every saved credential in cleartext. This is especially dangerous on shared environments like Citrix, VDI, and Windows terminal servers. Microsoft considers this behavior by design, citing that admin access already removes security boundaries. Security researchers dispute this framing, noting that Chrome's App Bound Encryption (ABE) only decrypts credentials when needed — and since Edge is Chromium-based, adopting the same approach is technically feasible. Mitigations include disabling Edge's built-in password manager via group policy, using a dedicated password manager, limiting admin privileges, and monitoring for memory-scraping activity.

recent_posts.title: CloudZ malware uses Microsoft Phone Link to steal SMS one-time passwords
recent_posts.summary: Cisco Talos has uncovered a malware campaign using a .NET RAT called CloudZ and a plugin named Pheno to steal SMS-based one-time passwords from enterprise Windows machines. The attack exploits Microsoft Phone Link, a built-in Windows app that mirrors smartphone messages to the desktop, allowing Pheno to read OTPs directly from its local SQLite database without ever compromising the victim's phone. The infection chain begins with a fake ScreenConnect update, drops a Rust-compiled loader, installs CloudZ with persistence via a scheduled task, and includes anti-analysis checks. Talos has released detection signatures and IOCs, and recommends migrating away from SMS OTPs to phishing-resistant hardware security keys.

recent_posts.title: Haun Ventures raises $1B across two new funds, betting on AI agents and financial infrastructure
recent_posts.summary: Katie Haun has closed $1 billion across two new Haun Ventures funds, expanding the firm's focus from crypto into AI agents and financial infrastructure. The raise is backed by strong first-fund exits — Stripe acquired Bridge for $1.1B and Mastercard acquired BVNK for $1.8B. The new thesis centers on three bets: new financial rails (including Erebor, Palmer Luckey's FDIC-approved digital bank), new asset classes like tokenized equities and prediction markets, and the emerging agentic economy where AI agents transact autonomously. Haun's regulatory background as a former federal prosecutor is positioned as a key differentiator as AI-driven financial activity raises questions around privacy, provenance, and trust.

recent_posts.title: Cerebras Systems IPO: $3.5bn raise, $26.6bn valuation, and an OpenAI deal at the center of it all
recent_posts.summary: Cerebras Systems is preparing to list on Nasdaq (ticker: CBRS), selling 28 million shares at $115–$125 each, targeting a $3.5 billion raise at a $26.6 billion valuation. The IPO is anchored by a $10 billion+ multi-year compute agreement with OpenAI, which also loaned Cerebras $1 billion and holds warrants for 33 million shares. Cerebras makes the Wafer-Scale Engine 3, an AI chip that places an entire processor on a single silicon wafer for faster inference at lower power. The company reported $510 million in 2025 revenue (up 76% YoY) but is not yet consistently profitable. The offering is reportedly 3x oversubscribed with ~$10 billion in orders. The IPO was previously delayed by a CFIUS review of Abu Dhabi-based G42, which was cleared in March 2025 after G42 divested Chinese investments.

recent_posts.title: AMD adds HDMI 2.1 FRL support to the Linux amdgpu driver
recent_posts.summary: AMD has submitted kernel patches adding HDMI Fixed Rate Link (FRL) support to the amdgpu Linux graphics driver, targeting the Linux v7.2 merge window. FRL is the physical layer enabling HDMI 2.1's full 48Gbps bandwidth, required for 4K at high frame rates and VRR on TVs. Notably, the HDMI Forum has historically blocked AMD from open-sourcing its HDMI 2.1 implementation due to IP licensing restrictions, making this a meaningful step forward. However, VRR and DSC support are not included in this batch — DSC is still being tested. The timing is relevant for Valve's upcoming Steam Machine, which runs Linux and relies on HDMI for TV connectivity since most TVs lack DisplayPort. Whether the HDMI Forum's licensing issues are fully resolved or merely worked around remains unclear.

recent_posts.title: UC Berkeley and Cal State East Bay students built real projects at OpenAI's Codex Creator Challenge
recent_posts.summary: Students from UC Berkeley and Cal State East Bay participated in the Codex Creator Challenge, a hackathon organized by OpenAI and Handshake. Teams built practical tools like campaign trackers and financial planners using OpenAI's Codex code-generation model. The event highlights a growing push to get early-career developers building with AI tools before entering the workforce, though the distinction between using a tool and truly understanding it remains an open question.
